_comment: Copied to <repo>/.agentkit.json by install.py. Every key is optional; scripts fall back to these defaults. Keys starting with _ are comments.

git._protected_commit: ask = agent must get your yes (default) | allow = no question | block = always refuse

notes._commit_tasks: false = notes/tasks/ (task notes + plans) is gitignored; decisions.md is committed

context._ignore_dirs: added to the built-in list (.git, node_modules, .venv, __pycache__, dist, build, wandb, mlruns, checkpoints …)
context._zone_max_files: rmap --zone prints at most this many zone files before '… +k more'

debug._min_similarity: dbg open/similar flag a past bug when keyword overlap (0-1) reaches this and >=2 words are shared

verify._comment: "auto" = detect · a command string = use it · null = skip this gate

guards._comment: Read by scripts/*.sh (install.py --guards). git.protected_branches, git.protected_commit, notes.dir and notes.base_branch above are used too. false switches a stage off; a missing tool fails its stage.
guards._ruff_cmd: command for the lint stage (split on spaces, no quoting): ruff check --quiet --output-format concise . ; ruff format --check .
guards._pytest_args: extra pytest arguments, e.g. --cov=src ; the coverage report is always --cov --cov-report=xml:<coverage_xml>
guards._fail_under: minimum coverage (%) of the lines changed against the base branch
guards._scope_ignore: globs the scope check never reports; null = built-in list (.agentkit/*, .agentkit.json, <notes.dir>/*, FAILURES.md, coverage files)
guards._hook_stages: stages verify.sh runs from the Stop hook (--hook); null = all. Names: lint, tests, diff-cover, scope
guards._push_stages: stages verify.sh runs from pre-push (--push); null = all. verify.sh --stages a,b overrides both
guards._destructive: ask | block | allow: what happens on git reset --hard, branch -D, clean -f, stash drop, checkout -- <path>, restore, push --delete, filter-branch, update-ref -d, reflog expire, gc --prune=now, force push to an unprotected branch, and on rm/mv/truncate/dd/sed -i whose target holds an unresolved variable. A force push to a protected branch is always blocked
guards._merge_convention: free text shown in merge/push block messages, e.g. "merge commit named feat(<scope>): merge X"
guards._require_merge_commits: pre-push: every first-parent commit pushed to a protected branch must be a merge commit

fs._comment: Files outside the repo, read by scripts/guard.py (PreToolUse guard-fs.sh for Edit/Write/NotebookEdit and guard-git.sh for Bash). The repo is the git work tree around the working directory plus every worktree that shares its .git. Patterns are globs ({tmp} = the OS scratch dir, ~ = home, ** crosses directories; a relative pattern is taken from the repo root). An explicit empty list [] means none; omit a key for its default
fs._outside_repo_write: ask | block: what happens when the agent writes, edits or deletes a file outside the repo (Edit/Write tools, rm, mv, cp target, redirects > >> 2> &>, sed -i, tee ...) and the path is not in allow_write. The message shows the absolute path. AGENTKIT_HEADLESS=1 turns every ask into a block
fs._allow_write: paths outside the repo that are always writable (scratch space and caches)
fs._deny_read: files no tool may read: a Bash command with any word naming one is blocked, and install.py --guards adds them as Read() rules to permissions.deny of the Claude Code settings (Claude Code applies a Read deny rule to Grep and Glob too, best effort)
fs._allow_read: exceptions to deny_read (templates people commit on purpose); written as Read(!pattern) carve-outs, which Claude Code honours only for relative patterns
